title: 環境・建築系数理（再履修クラス）
subtitle: Math and Science for Environmental Engineering and Architecture
courseType: Mathematics and Science ProgramMathematics and Science Courses
educationalGoal:
Students will
(1) acquire the necessary mathematical knowledge of functions, calculus, and statistics for structural, soil, and fluid mechanics, materials, surveying, and environmental engineering.
(2) understand the importance of fundamental mathematics for solving problems in architecture and civil engineering.
(3) apply mathematical knowledge to various problems.
advice:
This is a course on the fundamental mathematics used in structural mechanics, soil mechanics, fluid mechanics, materials technology, surveying, and environmental engineering.
Students will apply the learned mathematics to analyze various phenomena related to architecture and environmental civil engineering.

Students are expected to
(1) deepen their mathematical understanding of exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions, and tackle real problems requiring the application of this knowledge.
(2) deepen their mathematical understanding of differentiation and integration, and tackle real problems requiring the application of this knowledge.
(3) understand basic operations and graph drawings and data analysis by using Excel.
(4) learn statistical data processing methods and analyze data generated in experiments.
(5) utilize the Math. and Science Education Research Center and the teachers of the architecture and the civil engineering.

This course should make it possible for students to apply their knowledge of fundamental mathematics to solve architecture and environmental civil engineering problems.
books: Textbook: "Math and Science for Environmental Engineering and Architecture",  KIT
requiredKnowledge: Knowledge of mathematics learned in Mathematics for Environment and Architecture (functions and calculus basics).
